name: Kitzbüheler Altstadt
kurzbeschreibung: The historic Altstadt von Kitzbühel delights with colourful townhouses in Inn-Salzach style, the Pfleggericht, and over 750 years of town history.
preis: Altstadt kostenlos; Museum Kitzbühel Erwachsene 10,00 €, Kinder frei
oeffnungszeiten: Altstadt 24/7 frei zugänglich; Museum Kitzbühel Di–So 10:00–17:00 Uhr
beschreibung:
Overview

The picturesque Altstadt von Kitzbühel – situated in the heart of the Kitzbüheler Alpen at 762 metres above sea level – is one of Tyrol's most charming and best-preserved historic town centres. Shaped by more than 750 years of history as a wealthy mining and trading hub, the heritage-listed ensemble captivates visitors with its characteristic Inn-Salzach-Architektur: colourful townhouses with curved gables, broad battlements, and stately bay windows line the car-free pedestrian zone of the Vorderstadt and Hinterstadt, lending the legendary chamois town its world-famous sophisticated flair.

History & Architecture

The town's origins reach back centuries: copper was mined in the surrounding mountains as early as the Bronze Age. On 6 June 1271, Duke Ludwig II. der Strenge von Bayern granted town privileges to Kitzbühel. In 1504, following the War of the Succession of Landshut under Kaiser Maximilian I., the town became permanently part of the County of Tyrol. Kitzbühel experienced its economic zenith in the 16th century thanks to lucrative silver and copper mining at Röhrebühel, which financed the magnificent patrician houses of the townspeople. The architectural centrepiece is the curved Vorderstadt with the historic town hall and the late-medieval Pfleggericht (built from 1531), which today houses the Museum Kitzbühel. The museum showcases municipal and winter sports history as well as the world's largest collection of works by renowned Kitzbühel painter Alfons Walde (1891–1958). Remnants of the medieval town wall and the historic Jochberger Tor gate recall the fortified past of the town. On the neighbouring church hill, the Gothic parish church of St. Andreas and the Liebfrauenkirche with its distinctive 48-metre-high tower rise into the sky.

Visit & Getting There

The pedestrian zone of the Kitzbüheler Altstadt is open year-round around the clock with free admission. The Museum Kitzbühel at Hinterstadt 32 is open Tuesday to Sunday from 10:00 to 17:00 (in summer on Thursdays extended until 20:00; admission adults €10.00, children free). Arrival by train: Kitzbühel is an ÖBB long-distance stop (Railjet/Eurocity); from the Kitzbühel Hahnenkamm railway station it is just a three-minute stroll directly into the Vorderstadt. By car: via the B161 (Pass-Thurn-Straße) or B170 to Kitzbühel; central car parks (e.g. car park P1 Pfarrau or Stadtmitte) are available around the old town.

Tips

The entire town centre is car-free and features flat, well-kept cobblestones easily navigable with prams and wheelchairs. Be sure to visit the roof terrace of Museum Kitzbühel for a glorious view across the colourful gables of the old town towards the Hahnenkamm. Every Saturday morning, the Kitzbüheler Genussmarkt in the Hinterstadt invites visitors to sample regional culinary delicacies.
